title: Deterministic Process
definition: A process that produces the same output every time it is given the same input.

difficulty_levels.beginner: Think of a recipe for a cake. If you follow the recipe exactly, each time you make the cake, it will turn out the same every time.
difficulty_levels.intermediate: In the context of knowledge harvesting, a deterministic process is one that produces the same CID for the same conversation. This is achieved by using a language model to extract concepts from the conversation and then transforming those concepts into a standard format, which is then used to generate a CID.
difficulty_levels.expert: The concept of a deterministic process highlights the importance of reproducibility in science. In a deterministic process, the same conversation will always yield the same CID, which can be used to retrieve the concepts extracted from the conversation. This allows for the creation of a verifiable and transparent record of knowledge. The deterministic nature of knowledge harvesting also raises questions about the role of randomness and uncertainty in scientific discovery.

extra_fields.insight: The deterministic nature of knowledge harvesting highlights the importance of reproducibility in science and the creation of a verifiable and transparent record of knowledge.
